native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In a PCA of twelve forms of capital over 39 hundred-year slices (correlation matrix; PC1 = 30.3%, PC2 = 19.5%, jointly 49.8% of variance), the symbolic-capital components - house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) - load on PC1 with one shared sign and closely similar moderate magnitude (oriented +0.23 to +0.30; ranks 5, 6 and 10 of 12; within-group range 0.07, the tightest of any capital form), i.e. they sit inside PC1's dominant pole together with copper/gold, pottery decoration and hoards rather than opposing it, and add nothing to it: PC1 behaves as a general temporal rise of capital (loading vector vs per-variable time trend r = 0.96), so symbolic capital follows the main axis instead of defining or contesting it. On PC2 the trio does NOT spread widely: although all three nominally share the positive side of zero, hatchets/swords (+0.054) and daggers (+0.074) carry the two smallest loadings in the whole matrix (ranks 12 and 10) and only house size (+0.327, rank 5) registers, giving a within-symbolic PC2 range of 0.27, less than half the economic group's 0.64, and a share of PC2's variance (11.6%) under half of the 25% expected by chance. Symbolic capital is therefore concentrated on PC1 and essentially orthogonal to PC2, and it is the least well represented group in the PC1-PC2 plane (communalities 0.27-0.43, the weakest after sickle), with the weapons' distinctive information falling on PC3 (daggers are PC3's largest loading, +0.59). Caveats: signs are convention-dependent (the 37-slice subset flips PC1's sign but not the axis, |cos| = 0.996), PC2's identity is unstable (loading agreement r = 0.77 across subsets; PC2/PC3 eigenvalue ratio 1.51), the covariance-matrix run leaves the symbolic characterisation unchanged (r = 0.99) but erases sickle from the economic contrast, and with stepped series the effective n is about 7 rather than 39, so PC2-level claims are not statistically secure.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load capital.csv with decimal=',' (comma decimal separators), index by CE = -BCE, drop BCE/group/color -> complete 39 x 12 matrix of 100-yr slices. 2) Declare sign convention (orient on largest-|loading| variable, ties by column order) before computing. 3) PCA by eigendecomposition of the 12x12 correlation matrix (columns re-standardised on the 39 slices), all 12 components retained; eigenvector loadings, structure coefficients r = v*sqrt(eigenvalue), communalities, |loading| ranks. 4) Group spread summaries (range, same-side test, share of eigenvector sum-of-squares vs n/12 expectation). 5) Sensitivity A: 37-slice subset shared with time_series_data.csv; Sensitivity B: covariance matrix without re-standardisation; both compared with sign-invariant r on loading vectors. 6) Circular block bootstrap (block = 5 centuries, B = 2000, sign-aligned to the observed loadings) for loading intervals, sign probabilities and group-range distributions; broken-stick comparison; AR(1) effective-n diagnostics for the stepped series. 7) Axis-meaning diagnostics: PC scores vs calendar year, vs mean of all standardised Z, and by archaeological period; PC3 inspection for the trio. Pollen openness deliberately excluded.
